name: Dishwasher Circulation Pump Winding Resistance
purpose: Verify wash/circulation pump motor winding continuity when wash motor fails to run or hums.
failureModes: Open (OL): failed motor winding
Very low reading: shorted winding
testingTips: Disconnect power and pump connector before testing
Some models use one motor for wash and drain — confirm which winding you're measuring
notes: Resistance varies widely by motor design (AC shaded-pole vs. DC) — verify against manufacturer spec when known

name: Dishwasher Drain Pump Winding Resistance
purpose: Verify drain pump motor winding continuity on models with a dedicated drain pump.
failureModes: Open (OL): failed drain pump motor
Very low reading: shorted winding
testingTips: Disconnect power before testing at pump connector
Not all dishwashers have a separate drain pump — verify design before applying

name: Dishwasher Heating Element Amperage
purpose: Confirm heating element draws expected current during heat/dry cycle on 120V.
failureModes: Zero amps on heat call: open element, thermal fuse, relay/control fault
High amps: shorted element or wiring fault
testingTips: Clamp on element supply lead during active heat phase
Typical elements 700–1100W at 120V ≈ 6–9A
notes: Verify against element wattage/nameplate when available

name: Dishwasher Incoming Hot Water Temperature
purpose: Verify hot water at sink/supply meets dishwasher minimum for proper wash and dry performance.
failureModes: Below 110°F: long cycles, poor cleaning/drying, customer habit or distant water heater
Excessively high: scalding risk, may stress inlet valve seals over time
testingTips: Measure at nearest hot faucet after running until fully hot
Run hot water at sink 1–2 minutes before starting dishwasher test cycle

name: Dishwasher Tub Thermistor / OWI Resistance
purpose: Verify tub temperature sensor or OWI probe resistance at a known baseline temp.
failureModes: Open (OL): sensor failure, wiring break
Reading far outside range at known temp: drift or wrong sensor type
testingTips: Test at room temp or known water temp and compare to manufacturer chart
OWI turbidity sensors use different test procedures — confirm sensor type before applying resistance bands
notes: NTC tub sensors vary widely by brand — verify against manufacturer resistance table when known

name: Dishwasher Float Switch / Leak Sensor Continuity
purpose: Verify float switch or leak sensor contact state per normal (empty tub) operating position.
failureModes: Unexpected open/closed vs. expected tub state: stuck float, failed switch, wiring fault
testingTips: Confirm expected switch state for an empty vs. flooded tub before judging reading
Some leak sensors are electronic probes, not mechanical floats — follow model procedure

name: Neutral-to-Ground Voltage
purpose: Detect neutral-ground potential indicating wiring fault, shared neutral issues, or improper bonding.
failureModes: Elevated N-G voltage (>2V): loose neutral, panel bonding issue, shared neutral load
Can cause erratic control board behavior and nuisance faults on 120/240V appliances
testingTips: Measure at outlet or terminal block with unit powered
Investigate upstream panel bonding and neutral connections if reading is elevated

name: Electric Range Element Amperage (Single Element)
purpose: Confirm a single bake or broil element draws expected current when energized.
failureModes: Zero amps on element call: open element, relay/infinite switch fault, wiring open
Low amps: partial element failure, poor connection at terminal block
testingTips: Clamp one leg of the element circuit during active bake or broil call
Use element wattage with I = P/V to sanity-check (e.g. 3000W @ 240V ≈ 12.5A)
notes: Single-element draw — not total range circuit load; verify against element wattage when known

name: Hot Surface Igniter Amperage (Glow)
purpose: Verify igniter draws adequate current to glow hot enough to open the gas safety valve.
failureModes: Low amps with visible glow: weak igniter — gas may not ignite or valve won't open
Zero amps: open igniter circuit, failed igniter, control board relay fault
testingTips: Clamp igniter circuit during ignition sequence
Silicon carbide igniters often need ~3.2–3.6A; silicon nitride types differ — verify igniter type
notes: Amp draw is often more diagnostic than cold resistance alone — verify igniter type and manufacturer spec

name: Gas Flame Sensor Continuity
purpose: Verify flame sensor rod/circuit continuity per de-energized bench test procedure.
failureModes: Open (OL): cracked sensor rod, wiring break
Note: flame-rectification systems need live-flame µA test — this is a rough continuity check only
testingTips: Clean carbon buildup from sensor rod before testing
For rectification-style controls, follow manufacturer microamp procedure when available
notes: Bench continuity check only — rectification systems require live flame µA measurement for definitive diagnosis

name: Microwave Line Fuse Continuity
purpose: Verify line fuse continuity when unit is completely dead (no display, no lights).
failureModes: Open (OL): blown fuse — find root cause (door switch fault, HV short, magnetron fault) before replacing
testingTips: Disconnect power before testing fuse out of circuit
A blown fuse is a symptom — inspect door switches and HV circuit before replacing fuse alone

name: Microwave Thermal Cutout Continuity
purpose: Verify thermal cutout / cavity thermostat continuity when unit won't heat or powers off mid-cycle.
failureModes: Open (OL): tripped thermal cutout — often from blocked vents, failed fan, or magnetron overheating
testingTips: Allow unit to cool fully before testing — cutouts may reset when cooled
Clear vent path and verify cooling fan operation before replacing cutout
